answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance arises from progressive identity bonding: newcomers begin with minimal rights and must build a verifiable history of honest work before gaining influence. Picture a willow tree slowly taking root in a remote oasis, sustained only by the nectar of repeated genuine peer attestations and non-collusive transactions. Fake identities cannot shortcut this process, as rewards and voting power remain locked until sustained integrity is proven, rendering mass sybil creation costly in both time and forgone opportunities.
